text:
Maya Patel: Heads up — p99 tokens/sec on the token-level SLO dashboard jumped in us-west-2 around 11:12 UTC. TTFT p99 also increased ~150ms. Anyone seeing a traffic pattern or infra anomaly? https://grafana.internal.redwood/d/abc123/token-slo

prometheus-bot: ALERT firing: TokenSLO_P99_Exceeded (severity=high) labels={region=us-west-2, stack=inference} - queueing p99 > 400ms for 5m

Alex Chen: I'm pulling the raw heatmap. Can you paste the range/panel? I want the tokens/sec by shard. Quick PromQL to get p99 token latency: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, instance))
```
Try tokens/sec: `sum(rate(tokens_processed_total[1m])) by (instance)`

Priya Rao: Oncall here. Autoscaler logs show a scale-down completed at 11:08 UTC then a burst at 11:11. Might be a late scale-up. Fetching pod events now: `kubectl -n inference get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp --since=30m`

Sasha Ivanov: Noticed increased NIC drops on hotshard nodes in us-west-2 from host syslogs: `eth0: tx timeout` spikes ~11:09-11:14. Kernel ring shows retransmits. Likely culprit for transient queueing.

Jon Morales: Also saw a routing config flip in the canary that bumped fallback weight to the larger 'redwood-llm-xl' variant at 11:05 (PR #4321 merged). That increases per-request tokens/sec and memory usage — could delay cold KV cache population and push TTFT up. Rolling back that canary would reduce token rate per shard.

Maya Patel: Ok so combo: scale-down -> slow autoscale -> routing change -> NIC packet drops = p99 surge. We should treat as multi-factor incident.

Alex Chen: Short term: 1) pin routing to last stable (rollback PR 4321), 2) manually scale inference pool +2 replicas in us-west-2, 3) mute noisy alert and create delta alert for tokens/sec spike.

Priya Rao: Doing manual scale now: `kubectl -n inference scale sts inference-pool-usw --replicas=12` (was 10). Watching pods create.

Sasha Ivanov: I've opened a ticket with cloud-networking: NIC drops look like driver regression on a subset of hosts. Host list: i-0a1b2c3d, i-0f1e2d3c. Adding to infra channel and tagging network eng.

prometheus-bot: Alert suppressed for TokenSLO_P99_Exceeded (muted by @Alex Chen) until 2026-03-18T12:00:00Z

Jon Morales: For medium-term: revert the rollout, add a canary guard that checks tokens/sec delta before switching model weights, and add a KV cache warmup for new replicas. I'll draft an RFC.

Maya Patel: Action items — Alex: rollback + alert tune. Priya: confirm pods healthy and TTFT p99 back to baseline. Sasha: follow up with networking ticket. Jon: RFC for canary guard. Posting runbook link: https://runbooks.internal.redwood/token-slo-incident

Alex Chen: Rollback complete, PR reverted. Watching metrics — tokens/sec down ~18%, TTFT p99 trending back to normal within 3m.

Priya Rao: New pods are ready, no CrashLoop. TTFT p99 back to baseline (~70ms). Closing oncall loop.

Sasha Ivanov: Network team acknowledged; scheduling host kernel driver rollout rollback for the two affected machines.

Maya Patel: Great response. We'll follow up with a postmortem if the RCA holds. For now I'll update the incident tracker and convert this thread into a short writeup. :thumbsup:
